mt.tool.title: Take quantities off a building model: open an IFC file and pick what joins the takeoff
mt.busy.rvt.convert: Reading {file} ({size}). A large project can take a minute.
mt.err.empty: {file} holds no elements with a shape to measure.
mt.rvt.off: This build does not read the model inside {file}. Ask the architect for an IFC export (File, Export, IFC in the program that made it) and open that here.
mt.rvt.why.old: {file} was saved in {release}. The .rvt reader in the lab reads projects saved in 2023 to 2026. Ask for an IFC export instead.
mt.rvt.why.family: {file} is a family, not a project: there is no building in it to take off.
mt.rvt.why.template: {file} is a project template: there is no building in it to take off.
mt.rvt.why.partial: {file} is cut off: part of the file is missing. Copy the original again.
mt.rvt.why.unknown: {file} does not say which release saved it, so the .rvt reader in the lab cannot read it. Ask for an IFC export instead.
mt.rvt.failed: The .rvt reader could not read {file}: {error}. Ask for an IFC export instead.
mt.rvt.empty: The .rvt reader found no elements in {file}. Ask for an IFC export instead.
mt.rvt.note: Lab preview. This .rvt file (saved in {release}) was read by an open-source reader, not by the program that made it: it found {n} elements and may have missed others. {boxes} came in as plain boxes. Check the counts against the drawings or an IFC export before you price from them.
mt.rvt.nofabric: Lab preview. The reader found only {n} elements in this .rvt file (saved in {release}) and no walls, floors or roofs: this is not the whole building. Ask for an IFC export for a real takeoff.
mt.boxes.note: {n} elements came in as plain boxes because their real shape was not read. They are counted, and their lengths, areas and volumes are left out.
mt.openings.note: Door and window openings could not be cut out of the walls here, so wall areas and volumes are gross.
mt.name: Model name
mt.name.help: Keep the same model name when a newer copy of the model arrives: its quantities then update the ones already in the takeoff, and your names, rates and assemblies stay.
mt.row.file: Quantities stated by the model's author
mt.cell.none: No element in this row gave this number.
mt.how: Where the model states a quantity, that number is used. Otherwise it is measured from the element's shape: a wall's area is one face with openings out, a floor's is its area seen from above, a volume needs a closed shape. A * marks a number that some elements did not give; hover it to see why.
mt.compare: Against the quantities already here under this model name: {added} new, {updated} changed, {same} unchanged.
mt.compare.gone: {n} quantities from the earlier copy are not in what you are bringing in now. They keep their old numbers; remove them yourself if the design dropped them:
mt.over: {n} quantities is more than the {max} one model can bring in at a time. Untick rows, or group by category.
mt.note.boxes: {n} came in as plain boxes and give no length, area or volume.
mt.note.some: From {n} of {of} elements; the rest add nothing.
mt.note.mixed: {file} stated by the model, {shape} measured from the shape.
mt.note.rough: {n} are curved or cornered: their area is half of all upright faces, ends included.
mt.note.open: {n} have a shape that is not closed and give no volume.
mt.by.size: Category, type and door or window size
mt.note.layer: {n} come from a layer: the element's face times the layer's thickness.
mt.view.label: The model in 3D, one colour for each row of the table
mt.view.hint: Drag to turn, Shift + drag to move, wheel to zoom, click a part to find its row
mt.view.nogl: This computer cannot draw the model in 3D (WebGL 2 is not available). The table works as before.
mt.view.empty: No element in this file has a shape to draw.
mt.view.lit: Lit in the picture: {name} ({n}). Click it again in the table to clear.
mt.view.cap: {n} elements are drawn as boxes: the model has too many triangles to keep them all in memory. The numbers are not affected.
